content.thinking: This looks like a classic memory leak signature: heap climbing steadily since 08:48 while traffic stays flat around 1200, no process restart, and latency worsening in tandem with rising memory—all without any recent deploys.

hypotheses.subject: io-shop heap (memory_used_bytes)
hypotheses.summary: io-shop's heap grew monotonically from ~460MB to ~1.38GB (of a 2GiB limit) starting 2026-09-24T08:48Z while request volume stayed flat at 1200/min and the process was never restarted; latency degraded in lockstep (p95 219ms -> 706ms, p99 ~375ms -> 1245ms) as GC pressure rose. That is an unreleased-memory leak in the long-running process, not a traffic or code change.

supporting_evidence.claim: memory_used_bytes climbs steadily with flat traffic: 2026-09-24T08:47:00Z,461859122 ... 08:51:00Z,593440692 ... 09:06:00Z,1077970634 ... 09:16:00Z,1376016149, request_volume constant 1200
process_start_time_seconds is 1790198206.903535 for every bucket from 03:17Z through 09:16Z - the process never restarted, so growth accumulates over process lifetime
WARN io-shop: heap at 1046MiB of 2048MiB limit ... heap at 1316MiB of 2048MiB limit (monotonic +30MiB/min)
Latency degrades as heap grows while volume is unchanged: p50 46->148, p95 222->706, p99 378->1245 between 09:06Z and 09:16Z
Every recorded change to io-shop from 2026-09-17T00:00:00Z to 2026-09-24T09:16:46Z. (nothing changed in this window)
Error rate stays at baseline (0.0-0.025) throughout, and logs show only benign 'ClientDisconnected: the shopper closed the connection' errors present before onset too

hypotheses.summary: Alternative: an untracked change (flag flip, config push or deploy not captured by the change feed) at ~08:48Z enabled a memory-hungry code path. Nothing in the retrieved windows records such a change, so this is speculative and only worth trying if the leak hypothesis does not fit.
